WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him

"Pul the king of Assyria came against the land" in Menahem's reign; Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver, "that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand", and "the king of Assyria turned back". 2 Kings 15:19–20

"In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria", took Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee and "all the land of Naphtali", and carried the people captive to Assyria. 2 Kings 15:29
Ahaz of Judah sent to him: "I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me". He went up against Damascus, took it, carried its people captive to Kir and slew Rezin. 2 Kings 16:7–9
Chronicles: "Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came unto him, and distressed him, but strengthened him not." 2 Chronicles 28:20

Chronicles: "the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria", and the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh were carried to Halah, Habor, Hara and the river Gozan. 1 Chronicles 5:26
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
The altar Ahaz saw at Damascus, when he went to meet Tiglath-pileser, was copied in Jerusalem; Ahaz moved the brasen altar aside and kept it "for me to enquire by". 2 Kings 16:10–15
Menahem paid a thousand talents of silver "to confirm the kingdom in his hand". 2 Kings 15:19
Ahaz called himself "thy servant and thy son" and sent the silver and gold of the temple and the palace. 2 Kings 16:7–8
Chronicles: he "distressed him, but strengthened him not". 2 Chronicles 28:20
Menahem raised the money from "all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty shekels of silver". 2 Kings 15:20
The people of Naphtali, Gilead and Galilee were carried captive to Assyria. 2 Kings 15:29
The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh were carried away "unto this day". 1 Chronicles 5:26
The people of Damascus were carried captive to Kir. 2 Kings 16:9

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Scripture gives no year or length of his reign; it dates him by the kings of Israel and Judah (2 Kgs 15:19; 15:29; 16:7).
ROGERS (1912)
Rogers numbers him Tiglathpileser IV, an older numbering.
BABYLONIAN KING LISTS
No years given[71][75]
As king of Babylon: "Pulu", two years, in the Babylonian king list; Chinzer and Poros, five years from 731 BC, in Ptolemy's canon (Rogers's tables).
One king: Pul was his name in Babylon
R. W. Rogers (1912); Ellicott's commentary (about 1880); W. E. Barnes (1899)

Rogers: the new king "was proclaimed under the name and style of Tiglathpileser in Assyria, and later under the name of Pulu in Babylonia". The Babylonian king list has a "Pulu" reigning two years where the Babylonian Chronicle puts Tiglath-pileser on Babylon's throne for two years. Ellicott's commentary: "Pûl appears to have been the original name of Tiglath-pileser"; Barnes takes Pul as the earlier name and Tiglath-pileser as the royal name of one king. 2 Kings 15:19 1 Chronicles 5:26 [76][71][72][6][98]
Two kings, as the KJV wording reads
John Gill (1748–63); C. F. Keil (1872); the Pulpit Commentary

Gill takes Pul as the king of Menahem's day and Tilgath-pilneser as the king of Pekah's day, the one who carried the tribes away. Keil speaks of "the Assyrian kings Pul and Tiglath-pilneser"; the Pulpit Commentary also treats them as two. 1 Chronicles 5:26 [54][3][44]
How translations render the verse
the KJV and the World English Bible; the Berean Standard Bible

The KJV reads "and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser", and the WEB likewise ("Tilgath Pilneser"). The Berean Standard Bible (BSB, a modern translation on this site, public domain since 2023) reads "Pul king of Assyria (that is, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria)". 1 Chronicles 5:26

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no year or length for Tiglath-pileser's reign and does not say how he died.
Kings does not say that Tiglath-pileser set Hoshea on Israel's throne; that is in his own annals.
Scripture does not mention his reign in Babylon.
Isaiah names no king of Assyria in his words to Ahaz.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

Scholars' viewThis page treats "Pul the king of Assyria" (2 Kings 15:19) as Tiglath-pileser, as the site's person data does. Rogers (1912) gives the reason: the king took the name Tiglath-pileser in Assyria and was known as Pulu in Babylonia. It is an identification, not Scripture's own statement; the views are set out below. 2 Kings 15:19 [76]
From the textChronicles spells the name Tilgath-pilneser; Kings spells it Tiglath-pileser. 1 Chronicles 5:6 2 Chronicles 28:20 2 Kings 15:29
From the textThe site's person data also files "king Jareb" (Hosea 5:13; 10:6) under this king. That too is an identification; see the question below. Hosea 5:13 Hosea 10:6
